record.paper_title: An algorithm for solving linear nonhomogeneous quaternion-valued differential equations and some open problems
record.original_question: Can one formulate and study fuzzy quaternion differential equations that provide a mathematical model for quaternion-valued dynamical systems with uncertainty or ambiguity, analogous to the role played by fuzzy differential equations in other real-world modeling problems?

evidence.quote: As we know, the study of fuzzy differential equations provides a suitable environment for mathematical modeling of real-world problems involving uncertainty or ambiguity [3]. Therefore, investigating the fuzzy quaternion differential equations will be an interesting topic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}$ denote the skew field of quaternions, i.e., $\mathbb{H}=\{a_0+a_1 i+a_2 j+a_3 k : a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in\mathbb{R}\}$ with $i^2=j^2=k^2=ijk=-1$. A fuzzy real number is a function $u:\mathbb{R}\to[0,1]$ that is normal, fuzzy convex, upper semicontinuous, and has compact support. Recall that fuzzy real differential equations of the form $x'(t)=f(t,x(t))$, $x(t_0)=x_0$, where $x$ takes fuzzy values, provide a framework for modeling dynamical systems with uncertainty or ambiguity in their state and parameters.

Develop an analogous theory of fuzzy quaternion differential equations. Specifically:

(a) Define a suitable notion of a fuzzy quaternion number, namely a mapping $u:\mathbb{H}\to[0,1]$ (or equivalently a quadruple of fuzzy real numbers, possibly with appropriate compatibility conditions) along with arithmetic operations (addition, scalar multiplication, and a fuzzy quaternionic product) that extend both quaternion arithmetic and fuzzy real arithmetic.

(b) Define a suitable derivative for mappings $X:I\to\mathcal{F}(\mathbb{H})$, where $I\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ is an interval and $\mathcal{F}(\mathbb{H})$ is the space of fuzzy quaternion numbers, generalizing the Hukuhara or generalized differentiability used for fuzzy-valued functions.

(c) Formulate the initial value problem
$$X'(t) = F(t, X(t)),\qquad X(t_0)=X_0\in\mathcal{F}(\mathbb{H}),$$
for $F:I\times\mathcal{F}(\mathbb{H})\to\mathcal{F}(\mathbb{H})$, and establish existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence on initial data under appropriate Lipschitz-type conditions, in particular for the linear nonhomogeneous case $X'(t)=A(t)X(t)+B(t)$ with quaternion-valued (or fuzzy-quaternion-valued) coefficients.

Carry out this program so that the resulting theory serves as a mathematical model for quaternion-valued dynamical systems with uncertainty.
artifact.status_search_result: Some progress exists. Yang–Xu–Qi (2015) studied the Cauchy problem for quaternion fuzzy fractional differential equations, and subsequent work on Hyers–Ulam–Rassias stability of high-dimensional quaternion impulsive fuzzy dynamic equations on time scales has been published. Fuzzy split quaternion numbers and related differential-geometric structures have also been introduced. However, a comprehensive general theory of fuzzy quaternion differential equations parallel to the classical fuzzy real theory is not yet fully developed, so the program remains only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: The Cauchy problem for quaternion fuzzy fractional differential equations
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results relevant to the Cauchy problem for fuzzy fractional differential equations in the case of bounded integral operators...
status_evidence.claim: Initial existence theory for quaternion fuzzy (fractional) differential equations has been established.

status_evidence.title: Hyers-Ulam-Rassias stability of high-dimensional quaternion impulsive fuzzy dynamic equations on time scales
status_evidence.snippet: Fundamental calculus results of high-dimensional fuzzy quaternion functions; stability of quaternion impulsive fuzzy dynamic equations.
status_evidence.claim: Stability theory for high-dimensional quaternion fuzzy dynamic equations has been developed.

status_evidence.title: Fuzzy split quaternion numbers and Frenet formulas
status_evidence.snippet: Concept of fuzzy split quaternion numbers as a natural extension of fuzzy real numbers; differential geometric properties.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational notions of fuzzy quaternion numbers exist in the literature.
